ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ARABIC LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which greeting fits when you meet someone in the evening? (1 mark)
   A. maʿa s-salaama
   B. masaa'u l-khayr
   C. sabaahu l-khayr
   D. ʿafwan

2. What does the phrase al-hamdu lillaah express? (1 mark)
   A. Thanks to God
   B. A question about a name
   C. A request to sit down
   D. A goodbye

3. How do you ask a boy how old he is? (1 mark)
   A. kayfa haaluka?
   B. kam ʿumruka?
   C. ayna l-kitaab?
   D. maa ismuka?

4. How is the Arabic word مَرْحَبًا read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. anaa bi-khayr
   B. sabaahu l-khayr
   C. marhaban
   D. maʿa s-salaama

5. What does the mark shadda tell you in the word umm? (1 mark)
   A. The vowel is long
   B. The letter is silent
   C. The letter mim is said twice
   D. The word is a question

6. Which Arabic sentence means "My sister reads." (1 mark)
   A. هَذَا أَبِي
   B. عِنْدِي أَخٌ وَأُخْتٌ
   C. أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ
   D. هَذِهِ أُمِّي

7. What does the Arabic word حَقِيبَةٌ (haqiiba) mean? (1 mark)
   A. cat
   B. cup
   C. bag
   D. book

8. What is imitative speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Reading silently
   B. Speaking without a model
   C. Writing from memory
   D. Listening carefully and copying what you hear

9. What does the Arabic word قِفْ (qif) mean? (1 mark)
   A. touch your nose
   B. stand up
   C. close your eyes
   D. write

10. Which sound is in the name of the day al-khamiis? (1 mark)
   A. a hard k
   B. a heavy d
   C. a soft s only
   D. kh, a throat sound

11. What does the Arabic word تَفَضَّلْ (tafaddal) mean? (1 mark)
   A. drink
   B. gift
   C. juice
   D. please, go ahead

12. Why are special occasions important for a community? (1 mark)
   A. They bring people together and help them to live in peace
   B. They make people quarrel
   C. They are only for children
   D. They are only for the rich

13. What does the Arabic sentence أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I drink water.
   B. I like bananas.
   C. I like juice.
   D. I eat bread.

14. What does the Arabic sentence أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ mean? (1 mark)
   A. I like bananas.
   B. I drink water.
   C. I like juice.
   D. I eat bread.

15. How is the Arabic word أُذُنٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. jism
   B. udhun
   C. shaʿr
   D. lisaan

16. Which Arabic sentence means "I smell with my nose." (1 mark)
   A. أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   B. أَسْمَعُ بِأُذُنِي
   C. أَنَا أَرَى بِعَيْنِي
   D. أَتَكَلَّمُ بِفَمِي

17. Which is a sign of fluent speaking? (1 mark)
   A. Speaking as fast as possible
   B. Clear sounds and a steady pace
   C. Long stops between words
   D. Whispering

18. How is the Arabic word سَمَاءٌ read aloud in English letters? (1 mark)
   A. ghaa'im
   B. samaa'
   C. matar
   D. mumtir

19. What can help a nervous speaker? (1 mark)
   A. Practising many times before speaking
   B. Speaking very quickly
   C. Not preparing at all
   D. Whispering

20. What are the three parts of a short speech? (1 mark)
   A. Song, dance and drum
   B. Opening, middle and closing
   C. Question, answer and test
   D. Title, picture and page

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give two polite words for interrupting or inviting someone to speak, with meanings. (2 marks) (2 marks)

22. Translate into English: jaddatii tuhibbunii (2 marks)

23. Write three instructions about the body in Arabic sounds with meanings. (3 marks) (3 marks)

24. Translate into English: anaa tilmiidha (2 marks)

25. Translate into English: uhibbu l-mawza (2 marks)

26. Give three ways in which a family can reduce food wastage at home. (3 marks) (3 marks)

27. Write four Arabic celebration words in English letters with their meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)

28. Translate into English: hal ʿindaka hafla? (2 marks)

29. Translate into English: shukran li-istimaaʿikum (2 marks)

30. Translate into English: nuhaafidhu ʿalaa l-bii'a (2 marks)

31. Translate into English: al-yawmu yawmu l-khamiis (2 marks)

32. Write four parts of the body in Arabic sounds with meanings. (4 marks) (4 marks)
pages.answers:
ARABIC LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — masaa'u l-khayr
   masaa'u l-khayr means 'good evening'. sabaahu l-khayr is for the morning.

2. A — Thanks to God
   al-hamdu lillaah means 'thanks be to God' and is often said when answering 'How are you?'.

3. B — kam ʿumruka?
   kam means 'how many' and ʿumruka means 'your age', so kam ʿumruka? asks 'How old are you?'.

4. C — marhaban
   مَرْحَبًا is read marhaban and means hello.

5. C — The letter mim is said twice
   A shadda doubles the sound of a letter, so we say um-m.

6. C — أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ
   أُخْتِي تَقْرَأُ (ukhtii taqraʾu) means: My sister reads.

7. C — bag
   حَقِيبَةٌ (haqiiba) means bag.

8. D — Listening carefully and copying what you hear
   In imitative speaking we listen to a speaker and copy the sounds, speed and tone.

9. B — stand up
   قِفْ (qif) means stand up.

10. D — kh, a throat sound
   The letter kh is a throat sound like a soft clearing of the throat.

11. D — please, go ahead
   تَفَضَّلْ (tafaddal) means please, go ahead.

12. A — They bring people together and help them to live in peace
   Celebrations bring families and friends together and build unity.

13. A — I drink water.
   أَشْرَبُ الْمَاءَ (ashrabu l-maa'a) means: I drink water.

14. A — I like bananas.
   أُحِبُّ الْمَوْزَ (uhibbu l-mawza) means: I like bananas.

15. B — udhun
   أُذُنٌ is read udhun and means ear.

16. A — أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي
   أَشُمُّ بِأَنْفِي (ashummu bi-anfii) means: I smell with my nose.

17. B — Clear sounds and a steady pace
   Fluency means smooth speech with clear sounds, steady pace and good intonation.

18. B — samaa'
   سَمَاءٌ is read samaa' and means sky.

19. A — Practising many times before speaking
   Practice makes a speaker calm and confident.

20. B — Opening, middle and closing
   A speech opens by greeting, gives the main information and closes by thanking.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: ʿafwan (excuse me) and tafaddal (please, go ahead).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each word with meaning.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: My grandmother loves me.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: irfaʿ yadaka (raise your hand), ilmis anfaka (touch your nose), aghmiD ʿaynayka (close your eyes).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct instruction with meaning.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: I am a pupil (girl).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: I like bananas.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Cook only what is needed; store leftovers and eat them later; share extra food; use peels for compost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sensible way.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example ʿiid (festival), hafla (party), hadiyya (gift), kaʿka (cake).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Do you have a party? (to a boy)
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Thank you for listening.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: We look after the environment.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Today is Thursday.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the subject or first part and 1 mark for the rest of the meaning.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example raʾs (head), ʿayn (eye), fam (mouth), yad (hand).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct word with meaning.
